extracted.intended_audience: college instructors/teachers of public relations writing courses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for setting goals, objectives, and a systematic method to evaluate student public relations writing assignments (news releases, PSAs, brochures, campaign copy) using consistent criteria and pre-writing/evaluation forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose — what the writing is to make the public think or do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the assignment gives enough information about the purpose so the writer can determine a clear message statement for each public; judge how well the copy advances the purpose of the public relations effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Persuasive strategy — how copy achieves its purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the persuasive approach used (appeal, timing, tactics); consider whether the strategy is appropriate for the stated purpose and publics and whether it is likely to influence the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publics / Audience definition
rubrics_metrics.description: To whom is the piece of copy intended? What public is to receive the message statement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each public clearly. Evaluate whether message statements are tailored to each public, whether important publics are omitted, and how overlapping publics are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message statements: appropriateness and unity
rubrics_metrics.description: How appropriate each message statement is for each public, and how much unity there is in the message statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether message statements for different publics interact and reinforce one another (unity) while allowing for different appeals/strategies; use examples (e.g., faculty vs students) to assess consistent underlying messaging across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message–Medium–Audience triad (holistic fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the three basic elements: message, medium and audience and their interrelationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the interrelated fit: start with message, then consider how to convey that message to each public via the most appropriate medium; check for coherence among the three elements rather than treating them separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium appropriateness and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: How appropriate each piece of copy is for the medium for which it is written and which medium will best reach/credibly reach the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess which medium(s) the public will attend to, the medium's credibility for that public, barriers to using the medium, whether multi-faceted approaches are needed, and whether the copy is adapted to medium constraints (e.g., radio vs brochure vs magazine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Style, format and presentation appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Style — the appropriate style, format, and presentation for the medium and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the style is right, the format correct, and the information presented so that the intended audience will receive and act on it; consider conventions of the medium and audience behavior with that medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (facts and mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy — the facts, grammar, spelling, and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require factual accuracy and correct mechanics. Evaluate whether technical or scientific information has been translated appropriately (not oversimplified so as to lose credibility). Note that PR practitioners may lack an editor, so careful preparation is expected; check for errors that undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and directness
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy should be written clearly, directly and correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability and clarity of expression; determine whether jargon was appropriately translated for the audience and whether the message is easy to understand and act upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and audience testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing copy with target audiences and with relevant experts; use of readability formulas to ensure correct level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the writer tested copy (e.g., with age group or professional community) and used readability measures to confirm the level is appropriate for both audience and medium; consider whether testing occurred before public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Creativity — originality in approach, strategy, and use of medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how novel and effective the appeal, presentation, and strategy are in breaking through barriers to gain attention; reward original approaches that are appropriate to the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness (overall impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness — why a piece of writing did or did not work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether all elements come together into an impact greater than the sum of parts. Recognize that this often relies on instructor professional judgment supported by the preceding analyses; consider observable evidence or rationale for likely success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of research/evidence-informed design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of social scientific research findings to guide message development and persuasive approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the writer consulted relevant communication and persuasion literature for guidance, understood limitations of controlled vs field research, and avoided unrealistic expectations of research providing exact answers; research should inform approach rather than dictate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness for multiple-message/campaign contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: How messages to various publics interact and reinforce each other in broader campaign contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assignments covering multiple messages or a campaign, evaluate interrelationships among publics and message consistency across media and publics; check for gaps or contradictory messages that could undermine the campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and social responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of ethics — social responsibility of the task and potential manipulation concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require students to reflect on ethical implications of the communication task and to examine management acceptance and social responsibility; include discussion of ethical issues when evaluating assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management acceptance / organizational feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of whether the communication plan is acceptable to management and feasible to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate realistic management constraints, likely acceptance of the plan, and practical barriers to implementation as part of the overall assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive improvement and learning over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure student performance by progressive improvement over time across assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent expectations across diverse assignments to chart students' learning; evaluate growth in specific areas over the course and use patterns to adjust instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment compliance and project management
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to assignment specifications, prewriting forms, draft deadlines and submission requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether students completed pre-writing outlines, met draft and final deadlines, followed format/length/specifications, and used the prewriting form to focus the assignment; these procedural elements affect final quality and should be noted in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evaluation chart plus detailed critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency of grading via an evaluation chart while providing detailed corrective critique on the student's copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the evaluation chart to give students guidelines and indicate weak areas, but do not substitute it for detailed corrections and formative feedback; the chart should highlight areas needing improvement and document learning trends.
